ORDERS OF THE DAY 
2026-122 This authorizes the Mayor or designee sell the City-owned property at 12 Water Street 
to Dori Schulberger of Westbrook, ME for not less than $50,000. It also authorizes the 
Mayor or designee to negotiate and enter into a Purchase & Sale Agreement for the 
sale of the property and to execute a deed and other documents necessary to sell the 
property. The City of Westbrook acquired several parcels along the northern side of 
the Presumpscot River from Sappi in April 2023, which included the land addressed 
as 12 Water Street. Following the acquisition, the City was contacted by Dori 
Schulberger alerting staff to her residence on the property and her family’s history. 
Her mother, Sharon Schulberger, obtained a lease agreement for the parcel from 
Scott Paper Company in 1980 and located a mobile home and later a shed on the 
property. The original lease terms outlined rent at a cost of $300/yr, though at some 
later date this was increased to $400/yr. Later, SD Warren assumed the lease and 
continued to honor the existing terms. Following the passing of Ms. Sharon 
Schulberger, her daughter (Ms. Dori Schulberger) assumed the lease and continued 
the annual rent payment of $400/yr to Sappi, and later to the City of Westbrook after 
the City acquired the property. Ms. Schulberger approached the City asking for 
permission to purchase the parcel. An appraisal of the property valued the parcel at 
$50,000, given site unique conditions and limited buildable space on the parcel 
combined with the construction easements and other conditions that the City would 
retain upon sale. Ms. Schulberger is obtaining a formal survey of the property at her 
own cost. This order authorizes the Mayor or designee to execute a Purchase & Sale 
Agreement and sell the property at the proposed price and subject to such other 
terms and conditions as the Mayor or designee deems in the City’s interests. The 
$50,000 in revenue would be assigned to the Riverwalk North Project. This property 
sale is supported by the Administration, received first reading on November 2, 2026, 
and is in order for final Council action. 
 
2026-123 This approves the 2026-2029 Collective Bargaining Agreement between the City of 
Westbrook and the Westbrook Essential Services Unit (ESU). This unit was 
established to separate twelve (12) positions from the existing General Unit, and to 
recognize them as a distinct bargaining unit represented by Teamsters Local Union 
Page 4 of 176
No. 340. This change provided an opportunity to develop a collective bargaining 
agreement that more appropriately addresses the compensation, benefits, and 
working conditions of these employees. This agreement defines “essential services 
employees” as those whose primary duties are necessary to maintain the continuity 
of critical municipal operations, public infrastructure, including but not limited to 
maintenance, operational, facilities, wastewater, grounds, and administrative 
support functions essential to City services, but excludes certain positions that are 
either per diem, seasonal, part-time, non-union, or otherwise excluded by law or 
included in another City union. In March 2026, the City and Union filed the necessary 
documentation with the Maine Labor Relations Board to formalize the removal of 
these positions from the General Unit and their placement into the newly established 
Essential Services Unit. The filing was accepted by the Board, formalizing the change 
in bargaining unit representation.  
 
As a starting point for the new unit, the City and the Union used the existing General 
Unit collective bargaining agreement as a template, providing a consistent 
foundation for contract language, benefits, and working conditions while allowing for 
provisions specific to the Essential Services Unit. A significant component of the 
agreement is the implementation of a new pay scale effective July 1, 2026, developed 
using salary market data obtained from area municipalities. Individual wage 
increases vary based on each position's placement on the new pay scale and the 
corresponding market data, with an average increase of approximately 5% across the 
unit to reflect market salary rates. Additional provisions include the following:  
• Annual Wage Adjustments: A 3% cost-of-living adjustment effective July 1, 
2027 and July 1, 2028. 
• Signing Bonus: A one-time $500 signing bonus for each of the 12 bargaining-
unit members following settlement and ratification of the agreement. 
• Benefits and Working Conditions: Updates to reflect current City practices, 
changes in applicable law, and organizational changes, including revisions to 
overtime, vacation and sick leave, clothing allowances, education 
reimbursement, and Maine Paid Family Medical Leave.  
 
The projected costs associated with the new pay scale, signing bonus, and 
negotiated wage adjustments are $51,375.31 in Year 1 (July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027, 
includes $45,375.31 for the establishment of a new pay scale and $6,000 for the one-
time signing bonus), $27,813.87 in Year 2 (July 1, 2027 – June 30, 2028), and 
$28,648.28 in Year 3 (July 1, 2028 – June 30, 2029), for an estimated cumulative cost 
of $107,837.46 for this three-year contract, excluding scheduled step increases and 
any additional costs associated with other agreement provisions. The terms of this 
agreement were ratified by a vote of the union membership. This agreement is 
supported by the Administration, received first reading on November 2, 2026, and is 
in order for final Council action.

of FY 2027. The City Council adopted Order 2021-121 on November 15, 2021, which 
authorizes City departments to accept and expend unappropriated funds (such as

2026-126 This authorizes an award of bid to Glidden Excavating & Paving, Inc. of Gorham, ME 
for snow removal services at the Riverfront Parking Garage and Downtown Parking 
Garage for a three (3) year period with a two (2) year mutual-option extension. The 
cost of services for the Riverfront Garage is $37,759 for Years 1-3, $39,000 for Year 4, 
and $40,000 for Year 5. The cost of services for the Downtown Garage is $33,642 for 
Years 1-3, $35,000 for Year 4, and $36,000 for Year 5. As outlined in the enclosed 
memo from Director of Engineering & Public Services Eric Dudley, Glidden has 
provided snow removal services at the Riverfront Garage for the last 20 years, and the 
City is confident in their ability to assume services at the Downtown Garage as well. 
The City previously handled snow removal operations at the Downtown Garage, but 
this allocation of resources delays snow removal operations along the Main Street 
business district and on Brown Street. Funds for snow removal at the Riverfront 
Garage are included in the annual operating budget, while funds for snow removal at

the Downtown Parking Garage are available in a Public Services Reserve account for 
Year 1, funded through the Garage Operations & Maintenance Reimbursement 
received through the settlement agreement with TDB, LLC, authorized by Order 2026-
55. In future years, funding for snow removal for both garages would be incorporated 
into the annual operating budget. This award of bid is supported by the 
Administration, and is in order for first reading.   
 
2026-127 This authorizes an expenditure in the total amount of $19,999.86 to Sherwin Williams 
of South Portland, ME for the purchase and installation of new flooring in the Media 
Center room within the Children’s Wing at the Westbrook Community Center. As 
outlined in the enclosed memo from Director of Community Services Greg Post, this 
room is currently utilized for children’s programming, including before- and after-
care, and vacation and summer camp programming, and the existing carpet is in 
disrepair. The Community Center plans to continue using this room for children’s 
programming when needed but expand opportunities to utilize and rent out this room 
as a multi-purpose game space. Staff have recommended replacement flooring 
which includes a turf area for an indoor bocce court, plank tile for a shuffleboard 
court/bowling lane, and carpet tiles for the remaining area. The Community Center 
solicited bids from three vendors for this work and received responses from Sherwin 
Williams (low bidder at $19,999.86) and Blue Dog Flooring of Westbrook (second-
lowest bidder at $24,104.93). The third vendor solicited (J&M Flooring) did not 
respond. Funding for this flooring purchase and installation is available through the 
Community Center’s grants and donations account, which has been funded with a 
variety of donations from sources including but not limited to Collette Travel, Friends 
of Feral Felines, Westbrook-Gorham Rotary, and Westbrook Warren Congregational 
Church. We are grateful to all donors that support the work of the Community Center 
as a gathering place for community and connection. This expenditure is supported 
by the Administration, and is in order for first reading.  
 
2026-128 This authorizes an expenditure of $8,970 to Career Management Associates (CMA) of 
Scarborough, ME for the Non-Union Compensation Study & Pay Structure Project. As 
outlined in the enclosed memo from Human Resources Director Joanne LePauloue, 
the City’s pay structure for non-union employees is approximately 15 years old. Pay 
structures for employees covered by a collective bargaining unit are negotiated for 
each contract, generally every three years. For non-union employees, the rates are 
generally updated on an annual basis upon the completion of all outstanding union 
contract negotiations, and targeted changes have been made to certain steps and 
positions based upon internal market benchmarking. However, the underlying 
framework is outdated and no longer reflects current compensation best practices. 
As discussed during the FY 2027 budget review meetings, funds to conduct this study 
and to develop a more sustainable and equitable compensation structure have been 
included within the FY 2027 budget. However, funds to effectuate recommended 
adjustments resulting from the new structure will need to be included in a future

retain upon sale. Ms. Schulberger is obtaining a formal survey of the property at her own cost.

ARTICLE 26 - STORM & EMERGENCY POLICY  
          
The business of the City of Westbrook requires continuing operations during all except 
extreme conditions, although the safety of employees remains a primary consideration. City 
government will remain open for business as scheduled, except in situations where 
emergency conditions, such as severe inclement weather, natural disasters, public 
disasters, or energy system failures, warrant closing or rescheduling.   
 
Only the Mayor’s Office of the Mayor has the authority to make decisions concerning closure 
of municipal buildings and operations. During an official closing, all  Unit employees, except 
those who are defined as “emergency essential,” will be requested to leave work, if they are 
already present, or not to report for work.  
 
Emergency essential employees are those whose duties and responsibilities are essential 
in carrying out critical operational or life safety services of the City.  General Unit employees 
in the public safety and public services divisions, as well as other positions in the General

maintain a normal schedule, whether during a snowstorm, other inclement weather, or 
emergency. Individual departments will not make decisions regarding closure, early 
release, or delay in opening .  The supervisors in each department and division are 
responsible for developing an internal communication mechanism to aid in communicating 
closure of municipal operations from the Mayor’s Office to employees. 
 
During a closing declared by the Mayor’s Office, full -time employees , who are not 
emergency essential, will be compensated at their normal rate for the time they would have 
been scheduled to work. In the case of a late start or early closure, the employee must have 
reported to work to be eligible for compensation for the remainder of the day . For example, 
if municipal operations close at 3  p.m., non-essential employees leaving at that time from 
City Hall positions would also be compensated for the remainder of their normally 
scheduled workday, until 5 p.m. If the City closes for a full day, employees will be 
compensated for that day at their normal rate of pay, to a maximum of eight hours. Essential 
workers who are scheduled to work, and who do work that day, will receive their normal pay 
for that period, without additional premium pay or compensating time off . Part-time 
employees, who are not emergency essential, will be compensated at their normal pay rate 
only if they were scheduled to work that day, and only for the hours scheduled to work.

Censuring City Councilor Anna Turcotte 
 
The Westbrook City Council believes that free and open debate between differing opinions is 
central to a functioning City government and ensures the best outcomes for Westbrook’s 
residents. Productive discussions are only possible where issues before the Council are 
evaluated based on their merits, and the positions and opinions of the public, other Councilors, 
and the City Administration are treated with respect. The City Council adopted its Rules of Order 
to foster discussion and debate; however, those rules are only effective when Councilors 
respect and abide by them. 
 
During the City Council meeting held on October 19, 2026, Councilor Turcotte breached the 
Rules of Order. Councilor Turcotte made statements that did not address the issue before the 
Council and instead directly attacked and demeaned the personal motivations and intentions of 
the City Administration, calling them “disgusting” and “corrupt.” Additionally, Councilor Turcotte 
failed to honor repeated calls to points of order. Statements and conduct of this kind violate 
Section 5 of the City Council Rules of Order, undermine the function of the City Council and City 
Administration, and do not advance the interests of Westbrook’s residents. The City Council 
strongly disagrees with and does not condone Councilor Turcotte’s statements or conduct. 
 
The City Council hereby censures Councilor Anna Turcotte for the above violations of Section 5 
of the City Council Rules of Order. The City Council urges Councilor Turcotte to reflect on her 
statements and conduct and to offer an apology to the Council and City Administration.

the President is absent and shall perform such other duties as may be requested by the

the Committees and their members and designate a Chair and Vice Chair annually during the 
first regular meeting in December.

I. Introduction & Project Understanding
Career Management Associates (CMA) is pleased to submit this proposal to provide
professional compensation consulting services to the City of Westbrook, Maine. We appreciate
the opportunity to assist the City in evaluating and redesigning its non-union compensation

executive-level positions. The City's existing non-union compensation structure was developed
approximately 15 years ago and has subsequently been updated through cost-of-living
adjustments and targeted market-based pay adjustments.
While these adjustments have helped maintain the competitiveness of individual positions, the
underlying compensation structure has not undergone a comprehensive review. The City has
identified several concerns, including relatively narrow salary ranges that limit opportunities
for employee pay progression, compression between grades, and insufficient differentiation
among positions with varying levels of responsibility.
We also recognize that the City has invested considerable effort in maintaining market
competitiveness through its own peer compensation benchmarking, including a comprehensive
review in 2024 and follow-up adjustments in 2025. Rather than duplicating this work, our
proposed approach will build upon the City's existing market information and focus on
developing an improved compensation framework.
The primary objective of this engagement is to develop a practical, market-informed
compensation structure that provides appropriate salary range flexibility, meaningful
differentiation among grades, equitable treatment of positions, and a sustainable framework
for future compensation decisions.
Our recommendations will recognize the City's established compensation philosophy, its
desire to maintain salaries generally within approximately 10% of the relevant market, and
the fiscal and operational considerations associated with municipal government.

progression, particularly for professional, management, and executive positions.
C. Midpoint Progression and Grade Differentiation
Establish appropriate relationships between salary grade midpoints, recognizing
differences in responsibility, organizational impact, and the City's internal hierarchy.
The proposed structure will seek to reduce undesirable compression between grades
while maintaining reasonable progression throughout the compensation system.
D. Market Alignment
Evaluate the relationship between proposed salary range midpoints and the City's
available market benchmarking information. The analysis will identify positions where
the proposed structure provides reasonable alignment with market compensation
levels and positions where internal equity, organizational considerations, or other
factors may warrant further review.
